title: North Bayshore Precise Plan amendment: increase residential allocation to 9,850 units
summary: Staff recommends amending the North Bayshore Precise Plan to raise the residential cap from 9,850 to 11,000 units and to require 20% affordable units in new projects. Study session Sept 22; council vote scheduled Oct 13. Staff report estimates 1,400 additional peak-hour vehicle trips without new transit; EIR addendum in progress.

title: El Camino Real protected bike lanes, Phase 2 (Castro St to Grant Rd): remove 62 on-street parking spaces
summary: Council to decide whether to proceed with Phase 2 of the El Camino Real protected bike lane, which removes 62 on-street parking spaces along a 1.1-mile segment. Staff report cites a 31% reduction in bike-involved collisions in Phase 1. Business owners petition (214 signatures) requests a parking study first. Estimated cost $4.2M, $2.9M grant-funded.

title: CSFRA annual general adjustment and proposed cap on pass-through of capital improvement costs
summary: Committee to vote on capping capital improvement pass-throughs at 5% of rent (currently 10%) for CSFRA-covered units. Tenant groups support; landlord association says it will reduce maintenance investment. Staff analysis: affects approximately 14,000 covered units.

body: Mountain View Whisman School District Board
title: Attendance boundary adjustment and possible consolidation of two elementary campuses
summary: Board is considering redrawing attendance boundaries for the 2027-28 year in response to a 12% enrollment decline since 2021. Option A: adjust boundaries only. Option B: consolidate two campuses (Bubb and Theuerkauf are cited in the staff report as candidates). Public hearings Oct 1 and Oct 22; decision targeted Nov 5.

title: Shoreline Boulevard transit-only lane pilot extension (12 months)
summary: Council to decide whether to extend the Shoreline Blvd bus-only lane pilot for another 12 months. Pilot data: bus travel time down 9 minutes at peak; general traffic travel time up 4 minutes; 3 rear-end collisions at the lane merge. Cost of extension $380K.

title: FY2026-27 mid-year budget: proposed business license tax increase to fund unhoused services
summary: Council to consider a business license tax increase projected to raise $6.5M/yr, earmarked for expanding safe parking sites and case management. Chamber of Commerce opposes the size of the increase; service providers say current funding covers about 40% of demand.
